abstract: Strong Hund coupling to a slowly varying magnetic texture generates effective curved-space electron dynamics. {We show that an elementary vortex induces the exterior geometry of the Ellis wormhole in a controlled far-field regime, with a characteristic scale set by winding and Hund exchange and a short-distance completion determined by the microscopic core.} {The exterior metric deflection scales as (q^2/J), and its leading scattering-phase contribution is isolated by varying the exchange at fixed texture and carrier energy. The {spin-texture Berry phase} produces a distinct Aharonov–Bohm contribution, maximal for odd winding and absent for even winding.} {The same exterior metric can be programmed in a designer honeycomb lattice, where wave-packet dynamics support the predicted incoming trajectories.} The magnetic vortex thus turns a topological defect into a tunable curved-space lens for electrons in quantum materials and designer lattices.
title: Wormhole geometry from a magnetic vortex
